request.spec:
When a grade has no rate in force on a date on a sheet nor on its parents, a sheet that was
cloned uses the rate of the sheet it was cloned from (and so on up that sheet's parents and
source).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
When a grade has no rate in force on a date on a sheet nor on its parents, a sheet that was
cloned uses the rate of the sheet it was cloned from (and so on up that sheet's parents and
source).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A cloned sheet now falls back to the rates of the sheet it was cloned from. In a clean `bin/e2e` run all 4 tests in the acceptance spec pass.

An earlier run showed one failure because I accidentally had two e2e runs going at once against the same app. In that run scenario 1 failed (audit lines out of order); in the other, scenario 3 failed. The clean rerun afterwards passed everything.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data** — new migration `V89__sheet_source.sql` adds a `sheet_source` table that records which sheet each clone came from. It is snapshotted like the other per-sheet tables, so viewing a past date also knows the source.
- **Cloning** — `SheetCloneRepository.copySheet` now saves that record whenever a sheet is cloned.
- **Rate lookup** — `RateRepository.ancestry` now walks: the sheet, then its parents (up to 3 levels), then the sheet it was cloned from with that sheet's parents and source, and so on. No sheet is visited twice, so a loop can't trap it. Everything that resolves a rate uses this one method (claim figures, rollups, statements, the rates list and snapshots). That's why the front end needed no change: the "rate today" display already checks each level in order.

**Worth knowing:**
- Only the sheet's own clone source is followed. If one of its parents was itself a clone, that parent's source is not used. That's how I read "that sheet's parents and source" in the request.
- Sheets cloned before this change have no source recorded, so they won't fall back.
- If you view a past date, the source's own source isn't available. Parents already work the same way when viewing past dates.
